segments.text: Since we have reached the end of the session, it's important to do the salutation one more time. The salutation in bharatanatyam is also called a tap and salute, an ancient practice done before and after every lesson or dance, followed in pretty much all Indian art forms.
You get to your samapadam posture, which we have just learned, and we hold our hands like this in front of our chest. And we're going to strike our feet starting off with the right just one time.
And then you take your hands from here. Bring it down and sit in full mandi. And the dancer touches the floor and touches the eyes, paying respects for Mother Earth.
And the dancer makes a salute to the god by placing the hands on top of the head and in front of the forehead, saluting the guru or the teacher, and then to the chest, saluting to our audience.

If you want to keep learning, please practice the adavus and the postures, and you can try the adavus in different speeds. And always keep in mind that you would need to stretch before and after every lesson.
Thank you so much for watching, and I hope you enjoyed this video. Happy learning. Happy dancing. Nandri.
